external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A loyalty scheme member who collects and spends points through the mobile app, or scans paper receipts at a store kiosk.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers collect and spend loyalty points through our mobile app.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: A member of the support team who adjusts customer balances by hand through the adjustments page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Support can adjust a customer's balance by hand when something goes wrong, through an adjustments page the points API serves.

processes.name: points API
processes.description: The one service that computes, records and adjusts points; also serves the support adjustments page.
processes.source_excerpt: The points API is a plain REST service and it is the only way anything touches points.
processes.technology: a plain REST service, JSON in and JSON out
processes.notes: The two sources disagree on exposure and the value is flattened to unknown with both claims kept. Loyalty platform note: "The points API is internal-only; the mobile app reaches it through the group's shared gateway." Interview transcript, Priya: "The phones talk straight to the points API over the internet. The gateway went away last year". The transcript is stated to be more recent, but recency is not adjudication.

processes.name: store kiosk
processes.description: Self-service kiosk in each store where a customer who paid cash scans a paper receipt to claim its points.
processes.source_excerpt: Stores have self-service kiosks where a customer who paid cash can scan a paper receipt to claim the points on it.
processes.notes: What the kiosks talk to was probed and not answered. Dan asked whether the kiosks still write straight into the points database; Priya: "The kiosks are Dev's team's area. I couldn't tell you what they talk to these days." The fact inside the question is not recorded as a fact: no kiosk-to-database flow exists in this model.

data_stores.name: points database
data_stores.description: Holds customer names, email addresses, balances and the full collect-and-redeem history. The old offers database was merged into it.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, balances and the full history of every collect and redeem live in the points database.
data_stores.notes: Priya corrected herself mid-sentence: "It writes to the two databases— actually, no. We merged those in the spring. It's one points database now." The corrected statement stands; no second database exists in this model.

data_flows.name: collect and redeem points
data_flows.description: The mobile app sends what the customer bought and asks to spend points against a basket; the response rides the same interaction.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the points API.
data_flows.data_description: what the customer bought, and collect and redeem requests against their balance
data_flows.notes: Authentication was probed and answered with a hedge, so it stays unknown. Priya: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." and "Honestly I could not tell you today what it accepts". A hedge is a speaker talking about a fact, not stating one.

data_flows.name: submit scanned receipts
data_flows.description: Each paper receipt is sent to the points API as it is scanned at the kiosk.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every store and they send each receipt to the points API as it is scanned.
data_flows.data_description: scanned paper receipts claiming points for cash purchases

data_flows.name: read and write points
data_flows.description: The points API reads and writes balances and history; it is the only thing that touches the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.

data_flows.name: adjust points by hand
data_flows.description: A support agent opens the adjustments page and adds or removes points on a customer's balance.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a customer complains, someone on support opens the adjustments page and adds or removes points by hand.
data_flows.authentication: a single login shared by everyone on support; the page records that an adjustment happened, not who made it

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: Where customers and their phones sit.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the points API over the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: store network
trust_boundaries.description: The network the kiosks sit on, in every store.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the store network.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: Where the points API and the points database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The points API and the points database run on the core network.

trust_boundaries.name: office network
trust_boundaries.description: The Leeds office network support work from.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Leeds office, on the office network like everyone else there.
